record.paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
record.context_brief: Direct and inverse problem for ordinary h-fold sumsets
record.original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, and let A={a1,...,am} be an m-element subset of G. For a positive integer h, define the h-fold sumset hA to be the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am with nonnegative integer coefficients λ1,...,λm whose total is h, and define ρ(G,m,h) as the minimum of |hA| over all m-element subsets A of G. If p is the smallest prime divisor of n and m ≤ p < hm - h + 1, is it true that ρ(G,m,h)=p and that an m-element subset A satisfies |hA|=p if and only if A is contained in a coset of a subgroup H of G with |H|=p?

evidence.quote: the h-fold sumset: hA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ N0, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
ρ (G, m, h) = min{|hA| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}

Conjecture 3 Let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume that m ≤ p < hm − h + 1. Then for an m-subset A of G we have |hA| = ρ (G, m, h) = p if, and only if, A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G with |H| = p.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively. For an $m$-element subset $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}\subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset of $A$ as
$$hA = \Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i a_i : \lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i = h\Bigr\},$$
and let
$$\rho(G,m,h) = \min\{|hA| : A\subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$, and suppose that $m \le p < hm - h + 1$. Prove or disprove the following: $\rho(G,m,h) = p$, and an $m$-element subset $A\subseteq G$ satisfies $|hA| = p$ if and only if $A$ is contained in a coset of some subgroup $H\le G$ with $|H| = p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is part of a body of open problems on minimum sumset sizes and critical numbers in finite abelian groups. While exact values of $\rho(G,m,h)$ are known in many specific cases (including all groups of order at most 40, and for cyclic groups of prime order via the Cauchy–Davenport / Dias da Silva–Hamidoune theorem), the inverse characterization for general finite abelian groups under the stated range $m\le p<hm-h+1$ does not appear to have been resolved. Searches did not return a proof or counterexample.

status_evidence.title: The Minimum Size of Signed Sumsets (Bajnok)
status_evidence.snippet: Bajnok exhibited an explicit upper bound for ρ(G,m,h) for all n, m, h; the bound is tight in all known cases (including all n ≤ 40).
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of ρ(G,m,h) is not known in general, supporting the open status of the inverse characterization.

status_evidence.title: On the inverse Erdős–Heilbronn problem for restricted sumsets in finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Inverse problems characterizing sets attaining minimal sumset sizes in finite (abelian) groups remain actively studied.
status_evidence.claim: Related inverse problems for sumsets in finite abelian groups remain under investigation.
